transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’ve just been having a harder time getting myself to do things. It’s not too terrible, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but I used to go to choir, do my quilting, visit people… and lately I just don’t seem to have the push for it.

Most days I end up sitting at home with the TV on low, even when I know folks are kind of expecting me. That’s probably what brought me in, if that makes sense.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

I don’t know if I’d call it depressed, exactly. I mean, I get a little low sometimes, sure, but I don’t want to make too much of it. It’s more like… I’m just not as up to things as I used to be, if that makes sense. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you lost interest in the things you used to enjoy, like choir or quilting?

A little, yes… I mean, I still like the idea of choir and quilting, I don’t dislike them or anything. I just don’t have the push to get myself there or start doing it like I used to.

Most days I end up staying home with the TV on low, even when I know folks might be expecting me. I know that probably doesn’t sound great, but that’s more what it feels like.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?

My memory? Um… I don’t think so, not in any big way. I mean, I forget little things sometimes, but I figured that’s just normal at my age. I haven’t really noticed it being a problem. Is that what you mean?
Have you been worrying a lot lately?

Worrying? Um… not too much, I don’t think. I mean, I have the regular worries anybody has, but I wouldn’t say I’m sitting around fretting all day or anything like that. At least, I don’t think so. Is that what you’re asking?
When did you first start feeling less able to get yourself to do things?
I guess it started after I retired from the school office… a little over two years ago now. It wasn’t all at once, really. Just sort of built up little by little, if that makes sense.
Did this start after retiring from your job?
Yes… I think so. It wasn’t like the day I retired or anything, but after I left the school office, it just kind of started building. That was a little over two years ago now.
Have you been feeling sad or down most days?
Sad most days? Um… I wouldn’t say most days, no. I have some quiet days, I guess, but I don’t think I’m really sad all the time or anything. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is.
Do you feel this change in your motivation is mainly because of retiring?

Maybe partly, yes… I mean, having the job gave me a reason to get up and go, so I suppose retiring didn’t help. But it’s not only that, I don’t think. I just don’t have the push I used to have for things I usually cared about, like choir or quilting, or going to visit folks. Most days I end up just sitting at home with the TV on low, even when I know people are sort of expecting me. I don’t mean to sound lazy… it just feels hard to get myself moving.
Over the past two weeks, have you felt down or low nearly every day?
No… I don’t think it’s been nearly every day. I have moments where I feel low, sure, but I wouldn’t say it’s like that all the time. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During the past two years, have you felt down or low more days than not?

Over the past two years? I’m not sure I’d say more days than not… I mean, I have my off days, but I don’t keep count like that. I don’t think I’ve been low most of the time, no. Is that what you’re asking?
Has this change made it harder for you to manage your usual day-to-day responsibilities?

A little, yes… I mean, I still try to do what I’m supposed to, but I haven’t been keeping up like I used to. I’ve stepped back from leading choir and from some of the senior-center projects because I don’t always follow through on what I said I’d do. It’s embarrassing to say. Some of my church friends check on me more now, just to make sure I’m alright or that I remember things. I don’t want to be a bother, but… yes, it has made things harder.
Have other people noticed problems with your memory?

I’m not really sure… I don’t think anyone’s said it like that, that I have “memory problems.” Sometimes people remind me of things, but I figured that’s just normal, you know, at my age. Maybe they’ve noticed a little, but nobody’s made a big issue of it. Is that okay to say?
Has anyone close to you told you they’re concerned that your memory or thinking has been getting worse?

Not really, no… nobody close to me has sat me down and said they’re worried I’m getting worse. They might remind me of things here and there, but I don’t think they mean it like something serious. At least, I hope not. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you been waking up much earlier than you want to and then unable to get back to sleep?

I don’t think so… not much earlier than I mean to. I might wake up here and there, but I usually just try to settle back down. I haven’t really noticed that being a big problem. Is that what you mean?
Have you been having trouble keeping track of bills or other paperwork?

I don’t think so, not really. I mean, paperwork isn’t my favorite thing, so sometimes I take my time with it, but I haven’t noticed I’m getting mixed up with bills or anything like that. I try to keep things together as best I can. Is that what you’re asking?
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t any clear reason to worry?
I don’t think I worry a lot, no… I mean, I have normal worries, like anyone does, but not for no reason all the time. At least I don’t think so. Is that okay—does that answer what you mean?
Have you noticed your appetite has been lower than usual?
Not really, I don’t think so. I eat about the same, maybe some days I don’t feel like much, but I wouldn’t say my appetite is lower than usual. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed that it’s gotten harder to think clearly or concentrate?

I don’t think so… not more than usual, anyway. Sometimes I have to take a minute to gather my thoughts, but I wouldn’t say it’s gotten hard to think clearly or concentrate. I think I’m doing alright with that. Is that what you mean?
Do you often feel hopeless?
No… I don’t think I feel hopeless, not often. I have hard days like anybody, but I try to keep going and not think that way. Is that alright?

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms began gradually after retirement, a clear psychosocial stressor, and consist mainly of reduced motivation/withdrawal with mild functional decline. The interview does not establish a major depressive episode (denies depressed mood most days, denies nearly daily low mood in past 2 weeks, no clear neurovegetative/cognitive syndrome), persistent depressive disorder (does not endorse low mood more days than not for 2 years), generalized anxiety disorder, or mild cognitive disorder. This pattern is most consistent with an adjustment disorder.
